aspects.name: Personal, family, and relationship context
aspects.digest: Crystal met Natalie at UWI in 2002; they remain close friends. She met Douglas at the Montserrat Film Festival on Nov. 12, 2020, and had been with him about three years by Mar. 15, 2024. On that date, Crystal was 46, a TV/film producer earning about $85,000, living in East Janethaven, Montserrat. Her parents, Kimberly (74) and Bradley (79), lived 12 miles away in Old Town. Her children are Francis, Michael, and Rachel.

aspects.name: Estate planning
aspects.digest: On 2024-03-15, Crystal planned to start estate planning by listing her assets and identifying beneficiaries. By 2024-12-14, she had scheduled a will-signing ceremony at Montserrat Legal Center, 12 Queen’s Road; the time was unspecified.

aspects.name: Executor selection and responsibilities
aspects.digest: On 2024-03-15, Crystal was weighing Douglas’s organizational skills against Kevin’s legal background and considered co-executors; no final choice was stated. After a 2024-04-10 disagreement, they clarified the role. Douglas accepted on 2024-04-15. By 2024-05-02, Crystal was concerned about preparing him and handling conflicts; Kimberly preferred Kevin. On 2024-08-10, Crystal and Douglas finalized Douglas as executor after six weeks of consideration.

aspects.name: Estate planning process, meetings, and completion
aspects.digest: On 2024-03-05, Crystal read “Estate Planning Basics”; by March 15 she was planning gifts and care provisions and preparing for attorney Stephanie and family discussions. Her family met March 25; executor preference (Douglas vs. Kevin) remained disputed. She reported 75% completion by May 1 and about 90% by August 10, with reviews planned for September 15 and October 15. In November she was finalizing with Diana by December 15. By 2025-02-20 she reported 100% completion and a complete binder; whether the will was drafted and signed was not confirmed. Next comprehensive review was scheduled for

aspects.name: Estate and gift tax planning
aspects.digest: On Mar. 15, 2024, Crystal sought estate-tax and asset-protection guidance, citing Montserrat’s $200,000 threshold and 15% rate; she also asked about a 12% rate. An assistant example estimated $36,000 tax on a hypothetical $500,000 estate at 12%. In Aug. 2024, she questioned beneficiary-change and appraisal impacts and planned to consult accountant Christina; assistant examples used 15% and unverified gift-tax figures. After a Nov. 2024 workshop and questions about gifting and exemptions, Diana’s reported 5% threshold increase from Jan. 2025 remained a concern in Feb. 2025. Last state: after co

aspects.name: Will drafting, contents, and personalization
aspects.digest: On 2024-03-15, Crystal wanted humorous, personalized gifts and celebration-of-life instructions, planned to gather family input, and asked for legal terms to be explained. On 2024-03-22, she planned to finalize with Stephanie, believing Montserrat required two witnesses. In April–May she considered and reportedly used WillMaker Pro, saving eight hours; her May draft named Douglas executor, Kevin alternate, guardians and trustee, listed assets and instructions, and included a trust and funeral wishes. Later records conflict: in August she planned digital updates but was also said never to have

aspects.name: Estate planning education and resources
aspects.digest: On March 15, 2024, Crystal planned to explore setting up a power of attorney for her parents to help manage their finances if needed. On February 10, 2025, she completed the “Advanced Probate Strategies” course with a score of 95%.

aspects.name: Children’s trusts, savings, and guardianship funds
aspects.digest: Mar 15, 2024: Crystal considered a $10,000 trust for Francis, Michael and Rachel from $25,000 savings; no terms or trustee chosen. Jul 28, 2024: agreed on a $5,000 guardianship emergency fund; by Aug 10 she questioned adequacy and considered $10,000, but no increase confirmed. Feb 20, 2025: she reported allocating $50,000, then increasing it to $60,000 for the children; she had not signed a will.

aspects.name: Trust planning and funding
aspects.digest: 2024-03-15: Crystal asked whether a children’s trust had to be separate from her will; the assistant said it is typically separate but can be referenced in the will, and described setup and funding. 2024-11-12: She asked about a separate trust for her parents if care costs exceeded the will’s $7,000 fund. The assistant outlined options and suggested $20,000+ initial funding as an example, not a decision. It discussed possible tax implications, flagged U.S. figures as unconfirmed for Montserrat, and advised professional guidance.

aspects.name: Assets, protection, and financial planning
aspects.digest: On Mar 1, 2024, Crystal began listing assets: home at 45 Coral Bay Rd, valued at $350,000; by Mar 15 she also listed $25,000 savings, $15,000 film equipment and a $18,000 2018 RAV4. Her draft will named Douglas executor, Kevin alternate, Stephanie guardian and Kevin trustee for Francis and Michael; it was unsigned. On Aug 4 her home appraised at $365,000; she worried about the effect on her will and planned an advisor meeting about adding a $3,000 life policy now or in 2025. Sample estate percentages were assistant-generated, not her decisions. On Feb 18, 2025, she set unusual-activity alerts

aspects.name: Scheduling and other personal topics
aspects.digest: Crystal’s estate planning first surfaced by 2024-03-15; she was stressed about a May 15 will deadline while juggling a $50,000 film pitch due April 10. Douglas accepted executor duties April 15. In 2024 she updated guardianship, inheritance, and digital-asset provisions; postponed a $3,000 life policy to 2025 and added a $7,000 parents’ care fund, worrying it might be insufficient. She chose Diana ($900) on Nov 8; will completion was then unconfirmed. By Feb 20, 2025, her binder was complete, and she said her will complied with Montserrat’s 2025 regulations and e-signature laws.

aspects.name: Digital assets, legacy, and cryptocurrency
aspects.digest: 2024-03-15: Crystal asked how to protect digital assets, including Adobe ($2,000). By 2024-05-02 she added account provisions, planned gifts of Netflix/Spotify to Francis and Michael, and a secure inventory for executor Douglas. 2024-08–11: added Dropbox backup instructions; added Instagram/TikTok provisions ($800) and instructions for $1,000 crypto; no crypto disclosure decision. 2025-01-25 Kimberly accepted the plan; Rachel helped with quarterly inventories from Feb. Last: Rachel to help manage assets from Mar. 1.

aspects.name: Gifting and charitable giving
aspects.digest: 2024-03-15: Crystal asked about annual gifts to her children and whether to tell them; no gifts or decision to inform them were recorded. 2024-05-02: Her accountant Christina suggested $15,000 annual gifts to reduce her taxable estate. Crystal was open to this, pending Montserrat rules, recordkeeping, and discussion with Christina. 2024-08-10: She prioritized guardianship instructions over maximizing charitable donations. 2025-02-20: Christina advised $15,000 per child—$45,000 yearly; Crystal asked how to implement it, but had not said she started. aspects.name: Estate planning attorney, engagement, and costs
aspects.digest: Mar 15, 2024: Crystal had never met Stephanie and sought help finding an estate-planning attorney and assessing fit. Nov 8: She chose Diana for her technology expertise over Stephanie’s recommended Scott. Nov 12: She accepted Diana’s $900 fee (Scott’s retainer was $1,200), was close to finalizing her will, and had tracked $350 in expenses; her monthly budget rose to $420. Stephanie planned to retire in Mar 2025, prompting probate concerns and a search for a successor. Diana’s service terms remained unconfirmed. Another record associates her estate planning with Stephanie, not Diana.

aspects.name: Guardianship, guardians, and court approval
aspects.digest: 2024-04-28: Crystal said she named Stephanie guardian for Francis and Michael. 2024-05-02: She wanted Stephanie’s consent and considered Kevin as an unconfirmed alternate. By 2024-08-07 she had added school and medical duties to her will; she planned to review them with Stephanie. Stephanie said Montserrat requires probate-court approval; she advised notarized affidavits (repeated 2024-11-12). No court filing or approval is confirmed.

aspects.name: Will execution, validity, and filing
aspects.digest: On May 2, 2024, Crystal had not signed her will and was concerned whether two non-beneficiary witnesses were required; Stephanie’s review had not established validity. In November, Crystal said Diana confirmed electronic wills were accepted and also said they were required; the assistant asserted two witnesses could sign electronically, unconfirmed. Diana described an e-filing system launched in October, reducing processing time 20%. On February 12, 2025, Crystal said her will complied with 2025 rules; she filed it electronically February 16, and the court received and accepted it.

aspects.name: Digital security and password management
aspects.digest: 2024-04-25: Crystal enabled two-factor authentication on all online accounts and felt safer. 2024-11-07: She implemented 1Password for digital-estate credentials; on 2024-11-09 she helped Natalie test it, and by 2024-11-12 said passwords were synced and she felt pretty good. Further protections, including shared vaults, an emergency kit and account reviews, were recommended but not confirmed completed.

aspects.name: Will beneficiaries and inheritance distribution
aspects.digest: On 2024-05-02, Crystal considered naming Douglas after his $500 gift card and proposed shares totaling only 80%: 40% to her children, 20% Douglas, 10% parents, 10% charity. On 2024-08-05–10, she updated her plan to increase the children’s share by 10% and reduce charity, choosing to prioritize their security and consult attorney Stephanie; the assistant described a 50/20/10/0 allocation, not independently confirmed by Crystal. On 2024-11-12 she asked about advance notice for a crypto transfer. By 2025-02-20, she favored balanced shares and declined Erica’s request; she asked whom to notify, im

aspects.name: Probate and post-filing administration
aspects.digest: On May 2, 2024, Crystal said Stephanie estimated Montserrat probate at 6–9 months; Crystal sought help preparing her estate documents and asked whether careful planning could reduce it to 5–7 months. She had never used digital will software such as WillMaker Pro. On Feb. 20, 2025, after Crystal reported filing her will, the assistant recommended securing copies, informing executor Douglas and beneficiaries, organizing records, and consulting attorney Diana and tax advisor Christina; these were suggestions, not confirmed actions.

aspects.name: Estate documents and organization
aspects.digest: Estate-document organization first came up May 2, 2024, when Crystal asked how to work with Dwayne, who offered to help organize her asset documents by May 5. On Nov. 1, Bradley suggested setting aside $7,000 for her parents’ care in her will updates; Crystal began organizing her estate Nov. 3 and aimed to complete a full binder by Dec. 1, 2024.

aspects.name: Will updates, review, and compliance
aspects.digest: 2024-05-02: Crystal asked about making small will edits without consulting Stephanie each time; advice was to use WillMaker Pro for minor changes, seek legal help for complex changes, and properly execute and store revisions. In Aug 2024, she balanced updates with a film deadline; scheduling and review with Stephanie were suggested, not confirmed. Kevin, a paralegal friend, offered to review her draft. On 2024-10-15, she scheduled a review and wanted Vimeo instructions and digital assets included. By 2024-11-12, she preferred e-signatures. On 2025-02-20, she said her will included Erica and Ra

aspects.name: Software-version details
aspects.digest: On May 2, 2024, Crystal asked that answers about digital asset management tools always include software version details. The assistant gave WillMaker Pro version 2024.1 in its response; this was the version stated in the answer, not independently verified.
